text: cool i restarted the app with rebuild, i see what looks to be the start of what you did, but its behind a very annoying ui. [Image #1] lets do better here. zoom out for a second from just the actual world itself and this is where react becomes useful. you have this entire toolbar right above the map editor space to use and i can tell you didnt take any advantage of it [Image #3]
resolution: Map Paint's chrome moved out of the viewport and into the workspace action bar it was ignoring (cfffcd7da, hot-pushed live). The bar follows the toolbar's own conventions: PAINT toggle at the left of the world toolset; while painting the tool owns the row as a modal bar (the model-document branch precedent) — six channel pills, cycling SHAPE/PROF pills (the SNAP pattern), compact steppers, swatch-only tile/flora/zone palettes with tooltip labels, road lane steppers + COMMIT/CANCEL + draft readout, SAVE at the right; PAINT off restores the build controls. State lifted to the editor's real pattern: EditorState.mapPaint (the modelTool mirror) patched via AppFrame, with stage/mapPaint.ts as the one controller mirroring every change into the host tool; it now persists across hot reloads with the rest of the view. The floating dock is deleted — the viewport is clean (the loader's Ground chip is unobstructed again) and the brush beam is the only in-world chrome. No framework changes; pure hot-reload chrome.
